what: The whole panel is covered with sizzling film grain (three shader), and around the cursor the grain clears, leaving a clear hole that follows 1s late. Each cell adds time × .5 to a fixed random value and wraps it, and only when the value is under the .24 threshold does it draw a text-color dot of that value. Dots are not resprayed every frame but slowly switch on and off and twinkle (one dot stays on for about .5s). The hole has radius .01 and an 80× feather (fading out to about 30% of the screen width) and is mixed half and half into the grain value. At width 834 or less and on touch devices: no hole, threshold .25.

options.alpha: Threshold at which grains switch on (0~1), default .24 — higher is denser
options.alpha-narrow: Narrow screen / touch device threshold, default .25
options.radius: Hole radius (based on width ratio squared × 4), default .01
options.soft: Hole blur multiplier, default 80 — softens between radius × (1 ± soft)
options.mix: Share of the hole blended into the grain value, default .5
options.follow: Time (seconds) the hole takes to follow the cursor, default 1
options.narrow: Turns the hole off at or below this width (px), default 834
options.dpr: Render resolution multiplier when device pixel ratio is under 2, default 1.5 (grain is finer)

note: Dot color is --kf-ink × grain value (0 to threshold), so on a dark skin the dots are gray, slightly brighter or darker than the background, and on a light skin they are dark. After changing the skin, fire fx:theme on window to re-read it. With reduced motion, it draws one frame and stops.
